cases.answer: In TAILORED-AF, tailored ablation took much longer than anatomical ablation. Mean procedure duration was 178 ± 60 min versus 92 ± 36 min, and mean total radiofrequency delivery time was 42 ± 17 min versus 20 ± 11 min (both P < 0.001). The trade-off is that the tailored arm also had a higher periprocedural AF termination rate (66% versus 15%) and more patients achieved freedom from AF (158 of 180 tailored versus 124 of 177 anatomical, based on the primary-endpoint counts).

cases.answer: The network meta-analysis does not establish SGLT2i superiority for HFpEF mortality, and it contains no randomized head-to-head evidence. In the HFpEF network there were no significant differences between any drug classes for CV mortality, all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization/event. SGLT2i alone showed no significant effect on CV or all-cause mortality in HFpEF. The authors say the comparisons are indirect (placebo as common comparator) and hypothesis-generating, and that head-to-head trial evidence is lacking.

cases.answer: In the overall population, ΔGLS correlated significantly and positively with ΔPIIINP (r = 0.554, P < 0.001). Within the SGLT2i group alone the correlation was essentially zero (r = 0.013, P = 0.896), and within the control group it was also non-significant (r = −0.099, P = 0.365). The authors say the pooled correlation was driven primarily by between-group differences, so the parallel improvements in GLS and fibrosis markers do not support a direct linear relationship at the individual patient level. This weakens a mechanistic claim that fibrosis reduction mediates GLS improvement.

cases.answer: The advanced-CKD (stages 3–5) SGLT2 inhibitor cohort, in patients on ACEI/ARB, reported a significantly lower risk of ESRD/dialysis (aHR 0.35, 95% CI 0.19–0.67). It also reported higher genitourinary tract infection incidence (aHR 1.78, 95% CI 1.12–2.84) shortly after initiation, irrespective of prior GUTI history. There was no significant association with AKI or AKD. On design, the CKD study is a real-world retrospective cohort from a database (1:4 matched, 205 users vs 820 nonusers). The HFpEF GLS study is also a retrospective cohort (185 patients, 93 SGLT2i vs 92 control, median follow-up 12 months). Both are observational and non-randomized, so neither supports causal conclusions as strongly as an RCT. The CKD study is larger and database-based, matched on sex, CKD and program entry duration. The HFpEF GLS study is a single-hospital consecutive-enrolment cohort, with propensity matching as an additional analysis, and its endpoints are mainly surrogate imaging and biomarker measures.
